key_insights: In spring 2020 the University of Utah pushed its enrollment deposit deadline from May 1 to June 1 to give students more decision time.
Students must submit intent to enroll and pay the deposit before they can register for orientation, which is a prerequisite for course registration.
The counselor described herself as a one-stop contact who routes questions on housing, financial aid, and departments to the right office.
Students should monitor their official university email (accessed via the campus information system) rather than personal email, since missed university email was the most common barrier she saw.

The university has a standing deferment process (for missions, religious/humanitarian service, health/medical reasons) that was being expanded during the pandemic, deferring enrollment up to spring 2021.
Deferment still requires paying the enrollment deposit to hold the spot, and the decision to defer can later be reversed if plans change.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Enrollment deposit deadline moved from May 1 to June 1 (Sarah May Case, University of Utah admissions counselor, 2020)
Deferment allowed up to spring 2021 at the time of recording (Sarah May Case)
notable_or_distinctive: It is a COVID-19-era (2020) operational update specific to University of Utah enrollment logistics rather than general admissions strategy.
